files.why: Add framework-free `BillingPeriod` entity (id, name, start, end) plus a `BillingPeriodSummary` read model carrying computed totals/counts.
Add pure rules: select which invoices fall in a period's date range and sum their totals (reusing invoiceTotalMinor), then project to the period summary.
Add the server-shaped `billingPeriodDtoSchema` (snake_case, ISO date strings) so the mapper has a validated boundary type.
Add `toBillingPeriod` (and DTO round-trip) mapping ISO strings to Date, keeping DTOs from leaking upward.
Add `fetchBillingPeriods` / `fetchBillingPeriodById` doing real fetch + zod parse + mapper, matching the existing invoice query pattern.
Seed billing-period rows in server shape and add GET handlers so MSW serves the new endpoints against the existing invoice/appointment seed.
Add `/billing-periods` (list) and `/billing-periods/:id` (detail) route records; the app router already concatenates billingRoutes via index.
Load periods and expose per-period totals for the list view, mirroring useInvoiceList.
Load one period, its invoices, and join scheduling appointments in the range via the `@slices/scheduling` public surface (the canonical cross-slice pattern).
List named periods with their totals; lazy-loaded by routes.ts.
Show a period's grouped appointments and invoices with totals; lazy-loaded by routes.ts.
Add `fetchAppointmentSummariesInRange(start,end)` read model so billing can list the appointments that happened in a period (existing queries are by-id or upcoming-only).
Export the new range read-model query on scheduling's public surface so billing consumes it without a deep import (exactly worked-example #2).
Add unit coverage for the new period selection + totals rules, next to the existing pure-core tests.
Add mapping/round-trip coverage for the new billing-period DTO<->core mapper.

uncertain: Home slice: I placed this in the existing `billing` slice because 'Finance/billing periods' is a pricing/invoicing concern and a period's totals are sums of invoice totals. The alternative — a new top-level slice — was rejected because it would force edits to CODEOWNERS-protected `architecture.config.ts` and the structure test (`slices` set), which the README explicitly reserves for architecture review, not feature work.

Whether scheduling must change at all: if a period's appointments are defined only as 'appointments that already have an invoice', billing can derive ids from its invoices and reuse the existing `fetchAppointmentSummaries(ids)` — leaving scheduling/data/queries.ts and scheduling/index.ts untouched. The new range query is only needed if 'appointments that happened in it' means by-date (including un-invoiced ones), which is how I read the request.

Whether `billing/index.ts` needs modifying: not required for the internal list/detail pages (routes.ts is already re-exported and views are lazy-loaded). It would only change if periods must be consumed cross-slice or on the app ClientOverview.

Whether to extract a UI component (e.g. a per-period invoice/appointment breakdown table) vs inlining in BillingPeriodDetailView. Rule 7 says don't abstract before a genuine 3rd same-reason use, so I left component extraction out until the view demonstrably needs it.

Whether a Pinia store is warranted for periods. I assumed plain query functions (the README says reach for a store only when shared cached reactive state is needed); the single existing store is for the invoice cache.
questions: Membership definition: does the server define a period's members explicitly (period carries invoice/appointment ids), or is membership derived client-side purely from the date range? This decides whether the period DTO carries member ids and whether the scheduling range query is needed.
Which date determines membership — invoice issueDate vs dueDate, and appointment start (or overlap) within the range? Boundary/half-open vs inclusive endpoints matter for totals.
Scope of 'appointments that happened in it': all appointments in the range, or only ones that were invoiced? (Directly determines whether scheduling gains a new read model.)
Are periods created/edited/closed in-app (needs mutations.ts + create/edit UI), or read-only projections served by the backend?

What exactly are 'totals per period' — sum of invoice totals only, or also appointment counts/durations? How should mixed currencies within one period be handled (single currency assumed, or grouped)?
Where should periods surface — a standalone /billing-periods area only, or also linked from the ClientOverview and any global nav?
